newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - April 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - April 29.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Kuala Lumpur said yesterday a preliminary inquiry showed that no Malaysian Navy personnel were involved in the alleged abduction of seven Filipino fishermen from an island in southwestern Philippines. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- President Ramos directed Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo to take immediate steps to resolve the Monte de Pieded and Savings Bank crisis. (TODAY/INQUIRER)
- The hotel fire that killed 24 people and injured a dozen others in Cotabato city was likely set off by arsonists, the Bureau of Fire Protection said yesterday. (INQUIRER)

- The National Power Corp said yesterday it will reduce its selling rates in Metro Manila and the rest of Luzon effective this month due to lower prices of bunker and diesel used in power generation. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The European Union is expected to support the complaint of the U.S. against the Philippines in the World Trade Organsaition over the restrictive entry of pork imports, Trade and Industry Secretary Cesar Bautista said yesterday. (STANDARD)
- Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co's net income for the first quarter dropped by 1.8 percent to 1.28 billion pesos due to one-time payments for an ongoing manpower reduction. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
